Trainer-1

A 30 cm airframe on an 18 mm motor mount. Six parts, wood glue, one afternoon. It reaches about 310 m on a C6 and comes back on a 30 cm chute.

Kit summary
Apogee · C6310m
Dry mass85g
Length300mm
Build2–3h
Kit price
Coming soon
Motor sold separately. Pricing announced at launch.

Parts Manifest

Item numbers match the drawing
ItemPart No.QtyMaterialDescription
1TRN1-NC-011Molded ABSNose cone — Ogive profile with a pre-drilled shoulder eyelet for the shock cord.
2TRN1-RC-30140 gsm ripstop nylonParachute — 30 cm canopy, six shroud lines. Packs above the coupler behind the nose.
3TRN1-BT-301Spiral-wound kraftBody tube — 32 mm OD, 0.8 mm wall. Printed with a roll pattern so the fins line up.
4TRN1-AV-011FR4 · BMP280Flight computer — Reads barometric apogee, fires the ejection charge, logs peak altitude to EEPROM.
5TRN1-MM-181Phenolic + PLA ringsMotor mount — 18 mm tube on two centering rings, with a steel retainer clip. Takes A, B and C motors.
6TRN1-FN-0332 mm laser-cut basswoodFin set — Clipped delta. Slots through the tube and bonds to the motor mount for a locked joint.

Also in the box — shock cord, launch lug, ejection wadding, decal sheet, printed manual. Not included — motor, igniter, wood glue.

Build Sequence

2–3 h total · steps run in order
01Motor mountBond the two centering rings to the 18 mm tube, set the retainer clip, and let it cure before it goes anywhere near the airframe.25 min
02Fin alignmentSlot the three fins through the printed guide lines and epoxy them to the motor mount, not just the tube wall.40 min
03Recovery bayAnchor the shock cord inside the forward tube, then fold and pack the chute with wadding underneath it.30 min
04AvionicsSeat the flight computer on its sled and bring the arming switch out through the port hole.20 min
05Fillet and checkFillet the fin roots, apply decals, then swing-test on a string to confirm the stability margin before the pad.30 min
